source.title: Desorption and crystallisation of binary 2-propanol and water ices adsorbed on graphite
source.order_estimator: Mean slope of ln(I(T)) versus ln(relative integrated coverage) at a range of fixed temperatures; reported errors are twice the standard error of the mean.
source.order_class_note: Near-first-order fractional monolayer (n=1.23±0.03) and approximately zero-order amorphous multilayer; crystalline multilayer has a separate reported energy.

access_and_analysis.reason_not_run: Publisher PDF and figure-image endpoints were inaccessible in this assessment; no trace pixels could be inspected or digitized.
access_and_analysis.figure_pixels_retrieved_note: Search-indexed article text and Fig. 5 image were accessible; Fig. 2A digitization pixels were not retrieved from the publisher endpoints.

admission_requirements: Retrieve and inspect Fig. 2A under the stated CC BY 3.0 licence.
Digitize each identifiable 1-10 Lm monolayer trace and record axis calibration, overlap decisions and digitization uncertainty.
Freeze baseline handling, fitting interval, energy bounds and candidate-order set before fitting.
Use the reported 0.5 K/s ramp; do not invent measured time from temperature.
Compare production free-order and candidate fixed-order fits with the reported 1.23 +/- 0.03 order, noting the paper's distinct log-log coverage-slope estimator.
Retain failures and test sensitivity to plausible digitization perturbations.
limitations: The reported fractional order is not itself an independent software test.
The monolayer coverage-series order and whole-trace fitted order are distinct estimands.
The higher-coverage multilayer traces include amorphous-to-crystalline changes and are not a clean single-state zero-order case.
